description: Let the bundled dashboard, served from the local loopback server, set the zoom of the app's web views (`set_webview_zoom`, which Tauri's zoom shortcuts call on macOS and Linux; it takes any web view of the app and any factor) and call the app's own IPC commands: read/set the service settings (run in background, start on login, the server's port and how many days of runs its nightly sweep keeps), open external links in the OS browser, open a source file in a local IDE via its command-line launcher, open a dashboard URL (the trace viewer, an attachment) in a new app window, open and close the windows a run's output shows in (and, after a reload, those no run shows its output in), open a worker of a running run in a window of its own (which holds no native bridge itself), bring the dashboard window to the front once it shows a dashboard link the user opened in the system browser, check for and install app updates (read the release notes between the installed and the offered version, and turn the startup update notification on or off), show native notifications, forward front-end runtime errors to the server log, save downloads (bytes the page built, or a dashboard URL the shell fetches from its own server and streams to disk), ask for Playwright archives and bug reports to open (Ctrl+O on Windows and Linux), manage per-project linked folders (including read-only inspection of a chosen folder's Playwright/Piwi setup, and installing the agent skills into one), run Playwright tests in a linked folder with streamed output (and, after a reload, read which of them still run and how the others exited), take run requests from one team instance (keep and forget its key in the OS keychain, link the folders of its projects, and start a requested run with the command and request token the bundled server gives the shell), and render a run's live progress on the taskbar/Dock progress bar and tray. Added at startup scoped to the exact origin of the sidecar this launch spawned (`http://127.0.0.1:<port>`, set in place of the placeholder below) — no other site or local port is granted access, and only the desktop webview has the native bridge.
